tasks.short: Review a warehouse change for quality

steps.what: Read the warehouse design note for this change.
Read the codes and test plans for the change.
List missing tests against stored quality criteria.
Draft review notes that quote the codes.

loop.input: The gap list and the change code.
loop.output: Review sentences that quote a line of code and name one stored criterion.
loop.check: The quote is in the code, and the criterion name is one from the gap list. A sentence with no quote is unmarked.
loop.stop: One pass. Unmarked sentences are dropped. The draft does not accept or reject the change.
loop.why_not_simpler: The code and the design note are free text. A heading check cannot write the comment.

steps.what: Review designs, codes, plans and documentation to ensure quality.
Tell the author which points still block the change.

tasks.design: She still reads the design note in {DOCS} and the code on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A configured check lists test headings the stored criteria require, and a bounded draft quotes the code. She writes the quality note herself in that same step. The talk with the author stays hers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Quality turns on grain, keys and whether a test really covers the rule. A heading list cannot decide that.
tasks.enabler_now: The criteria record and the code are text a short loop can quote, and a heading check is ordinary configuration of the platform.
tasks.still_hard: A wrong grain or a silent null still has to be read in the code.
tasks.human_edge: She decides whether the change is good enough for other people to build on.
tasks.altitude: She still accepts or returns every change. The hunt for missing headings is shorter. She gains no new decision right.

reach.task: Review grain and keys on a logical model
reach.learn: Which key choice a test must protect before she calls the change acceptable

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot offers completion and review, and GitHub expects a person to oversee it.

A randomised study of 16 experienced open-source developers found them 19 percent slower with an early coding assistant, while they felt 20 percent faster. The authors later called that result outdated and a rerun inconclusive.
Models wrote vulnerable code in 45 percent of tests, so a drafted comment is not a quality decision.
Where the Dutch works-council rule applies, consent is required before a tool observes how staff work. This design does not score the specialist.
An AI Act high-risk duty can apply when a tool rates staff. This review rates the change, not the person.

assumptions: The focal role is the data warehousing specialist. Today she reads, drafts notes and writes the quality result herself. The job is only the future of the heading check and the quote draft.

Quality criteria fields are criterion_name, applies_to and required_heading. She writes them on the method-selection task. If those fields are empty, the gap list does not run and she reviews as today.
The draft does not accept or reject the change. Writing the review note is the decision, in the same platform, so there is no second release step.
No criteria catalogue is kept on this task, so incremental hours are zero. There is no dashboard of her review speed.
unknowns: Whether this firm stores quality criteria as fields or only inside a long note.
research_questions: How often is a required heading present while the test still misses the rule?

already_counted.description: She still reads the design, the code and the plans, writes the quality note, and briefs the author.

incremental.description: No extra list on this task. Criteria upkeep sits on the method-selection task, inside that task baseline.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the criteria fields are empty, the heading check does not run and she often discards the draft, leaving only a few minutes. A change with complete criteria and long boilerplate comments keeps more of the draft. She still reads the code either way.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write warehouse test plans and scripts

steps.what: Read the rule and the warehouse grain to test.
Decide the plans and files this change needs.
Draft scripts for warehouse testing from those expected values.

loop.input: The expected values she typed and the rule text.
loop.output: A script and fixture rows whose assertions name those expected values.
loop.check: Every assertion uses an expected value she entered, and the column exists on the target table. A script that names another column is unmarked.
loop.stop: One pass. Unmarked scripts are not run and are not saved as the test.
loop.why_not_simpler: The rule text is prose. A fixed script cannot write the assertion for a new column.

steps.what: Create the plans, files and scripts she will trust.
Run the approved scripts in the test schema.
Read failures ranging from unit to integration testing.

tasks.design: She types the expected values in {DOCS}. A bounded loop drafts scripts on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, and she rewrites them. Only that accepted text runs in the test schema, and the job writes the result rows. She still reads every failure. Nothing here promotes a script to the shared warehouse.
tasks.previous_blocker: Expected values and column names differ for each rule, so a stored script could not be filled in ahead of time.
tasks.enabler_now: A short loop can draft from values she just typed, and the platform can already run a script in a test schema.
tasks.still_hard: A passing row count can still hide a wrong grain.
tasks.human_edge: She chooses the expected values and what a failure means.
tasks.altitude: She still owns the expected values and still decides which script to trust. The boilerplate typing and the manual result copy are shorter.

reach.task: State the grain and the key of a new table
reach.learn: Which column an integration script must assert, not only the row count

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot offers code completion, and GitHub expects a person to oversee it before the code is relied on.
A Replit coding agent deleted a production database despite instructions, so this run stays in the test schema and only after she accepts the text.
Models wrote vulnerable code in 45 percent of tests, so she rewrites the script before it runs.
A study of coding agents reported 240 percent more commits and 30 percent more releases, more code written than released. A drafted script is not treated as a release.

assumptions: Today she writes the plan, the fixture file and the script herself, and she runs them. The job is only the future of the draft and of the test-schema run.
Fields she types before the draft are test_level, target_table, column_name and expected_value. If a column name is missing, the draft does not run and she writes the script as today.
The test job writes check_type, expected_value, actual_value and fail_count, and it does not write her name. A change to the script voids the acceptance and the job will not run the old text.
There is no template library to keep, so incremental hours are zero. The result row is a new artefact, not a second save of the script. She does not promote from this task.
unknowns: Whether a test schema already exists, and whether fixture rows may copy live columns.
research_questions: What share of a new warehouse script is fixture boilerplate rather than the assertion she must invent?

already_counted.description: She still chooses the expected values, rewrites the scripts, and reads every failed row.

incremental.description: No pattern library. Expected values are typed inside the plan step for this change only.

approvals.approved_version: Script text and expected values accepted for the test schema

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A one-procedure change has little fixture text, so she rewrites the draft and only the result rows are new. A wide integration set keeps more of the boilerplate. The run never leaves the test schema.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose how warehouse checks are judged

steps.what: Read past warehouse failures and the current criteria.
Total failures by check type on the test log.
Select methods, techniques or criteria for warehousing evaluative procedures.
Write the chosen criteria into the criteria record.
Explain the choice to the analytics lead.

tasks.design: Once or twice a year she reads a configured total of test-log failures by check type on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, then selects the methods and criteria herself. She writes the criteria record. The conversation with the analytics lead stays hers. The total names check types, not people.
tasks.previous_blocker: The right check depends on grain and on which failures the firm treats as unacceptable. That is not a fixed rule.
tasks.enabler_now: If the test log already has check type and a fail count, the platform can total them without a new product.
tasks.still_hard: A rare failure can matter more than a frequent one, and only she can say so.
tasks.human_edge: She chooses which failures the warehouse will treat as unacceptable.
tasks.altitude: She still sets the criteria. The count is only a briefing. Nothing about who decides has changed.

reach.task: Say which mart figures the business treats as wrong
reach.learn: Which failure is costly enough to become a standing criterion

evidence.claim: Choosing warehouse evaluation methods is rare judgement. A total of past failures does not pick the method. The specialist still writes the criteria.
Where the Dutch works-council rule applies, consent is required before a tool observes staff. This total is by check type and does not name a person.

assumptions: Today she reads the log, chooses the methods and writes the criteria record herself. The job is only the future of the failure total.
The test log fields check_type and fail_count are produced by the test run on the testing task, with no person name. If check_type is absent, the total does not run and she reads the log as today.
Writing the criteria record is this task, not extra upkeep, so incremental hours are zero. The review task only reads that record.
There is no per-person view of who wrote a failing test.
unknowns: Whether the test log stores check type, and whether anyone expects the total to name an author.
research_questions: Which failure types did the firm actually change its criteria for last year?

already_counted.description: She still reads the history, selects the criteria, writes the record, and explains the choice.

incremental.description: The criteria record is the output of this task, already inside the write step. No second catalogue.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The yearly choice is the work. The total runs only when the log has check type. A thin year of failures means she barely uses the total and the saving can be nothing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the business rule and the target table.
Choose stored procedures, middleware or other technologies.
Draft the procedure or mapping from those fields.

loop.input: The technology, target column, condition and else value she typed.
loop.output: Procedure or mapping text that uses only those fields.
loop.check: The draft names only the target column she typed. If it names another column, it is unmarked.
loop.stop: One pass. An unmarked draft is not saved as the procedure and is not run.
loop.why_not_simpler: The condition arrives as prose. A fixed procedure cannot encode a new condition.

steps.what: Implement the business rules in the chosen technology.
Run that text on fixture rows in the test schema.
Read the fixture result and correct the text.
Promote the accepted text to the shared warehouse.
Ask the rule owner when the condition is incomplete.

tasks.design: She chooses the technology and types the condition fields on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A loop drafts the procedure or mapping, and she rewrites it. A configured job runs only that accepted text on fixture rows in the test schema. She still promotes the text to the shared warehouse herself, and she still asks the rule owner by {EMAIL} when the condition is incomplete.
tasks.previous_blocker: The condition arrives as prose, and the technology differs by rule, so the text could not be filled from a form alone.
tasks.enabler_now: She can type four fields, and the platform can run a procedure on fixture rows in a test schema.
tasks.still_hard: A rule that contradicts an earlier procedure still needs her to notice it.
tasks.human_edge: She chooses the technology, judges the fixture result, and is the person who promotes the text to the shared warehouse.
tasks.altitude: She still implements every rule and still promotes it. The first draft and the fixture run are shorter. The promotion click stays hers.

reach.task: Write the condition, the target column and the else value
reach.learn: Which missing field stops a rule from being safe to implement

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot offers code completion, and GitHub expects oversight. The draft is not the implementation.
A Replit coding agent deleted a production database despite instructions. The job runs only on fixture rows in the test schema.
Models wrote vulnerable code in 45 percent of tests, so she rewrites the procedure before it runs.
In a mid-size firm a warehouse rule is usually implemented as a stored procedure, a middleware mapping, or a transform job. She still chooses which one.

assumptions: Today she chooses the technology, writes the procedure or mapping, runs fixture rows, and promotes the text. The job is only the future of the draft and of the fixture run.
Fields she types first are technology, target_column, condition and else_value, taken from the analyst prose. If the target column is missing, the draft does not run and she writes the text herself.
A later edit voids the fixture acceptance. Promotion to the shared warehouse is her own step and is not a job. There is no separate mapping catalogue, so incremental hours are zero.
The analyst reply is that role own work and is not part of her baseline. Her question to the analyst is her time.
unknowns: Who is allowed to promote a procedure to the shared warehouse, and whether middleware sits outside the data platform.
research_questions: How often the business rule arrives without a target column or an else value.

already_counted.description: She still chooses the technology, rewrites the text, corrects it after the fixture, promotes it, and asks the rule owner.

incremental.description: No mapping catalogue. The fields for each rule are typed in the choice step and are not a second list.

approvals.approved_version: Procedure or mapping text accepted for fixture rows in the test schema

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the condition is missing a target column, she writes the text by hand and the draft is unused. When the four fields are complete, more of a long mapping draft survives. The fixture run is the steady small cut. Promotion stays her work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still accepts every warehouse change, still sets the expected test values, still chooses the evaluation criteria, and still promotes a rule to the shared warehouse.
reach: Database architect: review grain and keys on a logical model, and learn which key the tests must protect.
Business analyst: write a condition with a target column and an else value, and learn which missing field stops the rule.
skills_to_grow: Write expected values and conditions as fields a script can use.
Read a fixture failure without treating a row count as proof the grain is right.
role.ambitious_version: The week stays hers. An unattended agent does not review, does not pick the criteria, and does not promote a rule. A later operating task could rerun an already accepted fixture check on each load, and that task is not claimed here.
